organization: Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada

plan_title: IRCC Accessibility Progress Report 2024
plan_commitment_excerpt: Guidance was reviewed and issued to initiate progress toward adopting a social approach to disabilities in alignment with the government's direction in that regard. This includes shifting from the default requirement for medical proof to be provided in DTA requests to ensuring that managers have sufficient documentation clearly identifying the barriers faced by the employee to support their request rather than their medical condition.
plan_notes: Reviewed through the 2024 progress report. IRCC also ran weekly coaching for case managers on the social model and produced videos on medical vs social model. Employees named use of the medical model rather than the social model as their top challenge (13 votes). The 2023 progress report has no mention.

plan_title: 2026-2028 Indigenous Services Canada and Indian Oil and Gas Canada Accessibility Plan
plan_commitment_excerpt: As part of this redesign, ISC is adopting a social model of accommodations for persons with disabilities focusing on removing systemic barriers rather than the traditional model which relies on medical documentation. This approach embraces a 'yes by default' mindset, for low-cost accommodation measures, where the starting point is trust and support, and less reliance on medical certification.
plan_notes: Strongest commitment found. Also includes Commitment 2, regular and ongoing training on the accommodation request process, the social model of disability, non-visible disabilities and the rights of employees, and a Duty to Accommodate redesign to better reflect the social model and the lived realities of Indigenous persons with disabilities.
